question.worked_solution:
First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So, we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Rearranging the above identity gives

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡x-1={tan}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3/2}\frac{3{x}^{2}{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3/2}\frac{3{x}^{2}{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3/2}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{3}\,{|}_{1}^{3/2} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2})}^{\,3}-{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{27}{8}-1 \\  & =\frac{19}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
